title: Hail to the Sabbath Day
description: Hail to the Sabbath Day in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 42 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Sabbath Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail to the Sab-bath day! The day di-vine-ly given, When men to God their hom-age pay, And earth draws near to heaven.

lines: When men to God their homage pay,
And earth draws near to heaven.
And bless thy love, and own thy power,
Nor only is the day thine own
When man draws near to God.
And purer worship may we pay

licence: Public domain: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch died in 1870.
credits: Words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
